To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the observed baryon rapidities in nucleus-nucleus collision can be explained by assuming that the baryon number conservation is not violated and by assuming a simple string fragmentation process.

(i) the baryon rapidities in nucleus-nucleus collision at ultra-relativist energies can be explained as the result of independent string fragmentation and diquark formation in the intermediate state, and (ii) the nuclear stopping power in nucleus-nucleous collisions can be explained as a result of a simple model for the interaction of strings with the target nucleus, which is based on the idea of a string being split into two parts by the target nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hadronic interactions at ultra-relativisitic energies.
a study of hadron production in the framework of the Lund model.
the development of a model of multiparticle-production processes at ultra-relativist energies based on the string fragmentation model.
